title: Favourites for signed-in customers
context: Signed-in customers keep a personal list of favourite products, from the product page (web shop) and through the API (mobile app).

sourcesRead.contributes: context (L17); technical notes: favourites endpoints, request body, Bearer auth from POST /users/login, 422 for duplicates (L19); AC-1…AC-6 from the acceptance-criteria custom field (L23-L28); PO clarification: duplicate → 409 Conflict superseding 422, web-shop duplicate message unchanged (L34)

acceptanceCriteria.text: A signed-in customer adds a product to favourites with POST /favorites; the API responds 201 with the favourite (its id and the product id).
acceptanceCriteria.quote: A signed-in customer adds a product to favourites with POST /favorites; the API responds 201 with the favourite (its id and the product id).
outcomes: the body is the favourite, with its id
the body carries the product id that was sent

acceptanceCriteria.text: Adding a product that is already a favourite is rejected and the list still contains it once.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: Adding a product that is already a favourite is rejected and the list still contains it once.
outcomes: adding the same product again with POST /favorites → 409 (Conflict)

acceptanceCriteria.text: GET /favorites lists the customer's own favourites only; another customer's favourites are never included.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: GET /favorites lists the customer's own favourites only; another customer's favourites are never included.
outcomes: GET /favorites lists the favourites the customer added
a favourite added by another customer is not included

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every favourites endpoint responds 401 without a valid token.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: Every favourites endpoint responds 401 without a valid token.
outcomes: each of them with an invalid token → 401

acceptanceCriteria.text: On the web shop, a signed-in customer who clicks "Add to favourites" on a product page sees "Product added to your favorites list." and the product then appears on the "Favorites" page of their account.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: On the web shop, a signed-in customer who clicks "Add to favourites" on a product page sees "Product added to your favorites list." and the product then appears on the "Favorites" page of their account.
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: product page of the web shop, after signing in (routes and labels: G5, G6)
outcomes: clicking "Add to favourites" shows "Product added to your favorites list."
the product appears on the "Favorites" page of the customer's account

acceptanceCriteria.text: DELETE /favorites/{favoriteId} removes the favourite (204) and it no longer appears in GET /favorites.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: DELETE /favorites/{favoriteId} removes the favourite (204) and it no longer appears in GET /favorites.
outcomes: GET /favorites afterwards no longer contains that favourite

endpoints.success: 201 with the favourite (its id and the product id)

rules.text: A duplicate favourite is a conflict: the API must answer 409 Conflict (the PO clarification supersedes the 422 in the technical notes).

errorModel.case: Adding a product that is already a favourite (POST /favorites)
Any favourites endpoint called without a valid token

auth.mechanism: Authorization: Bearer <token>, the token obtained from POST /users/login; required by all favourites endpoints
auth.credentials: a freshly registered test customer per test (G3)

testData.strategy: Register fresh customers through POST /users/register (G3) and sign them in with POST /users/login for a Bearer token; pick existing product ids from GET /products/search (G4). AC-3 uses two customers. AC-5 signs the registered customer in on the web shop (G5).
constraints: unique e-mail address per registered customer (run-scoped)
each test uses its own customer so favourites lists start empty and are not shared between tests
testData.cleanup: favourites created through the API are removed with DELETE /favorites/{favoriteId}; registered test customers are left in place (unique per run)

outOfScope: The message the web shop shows for a duplicate favourite: the PO says the web shop can keep its current message (story.md#L34), so no web-shop duplicate message is specified or tested

gaps.element: status for a duplicate favourite: the technical notes say 422, the PO comment says 409
